title: How squashed is the Earth?
hook: Diagrams show the Earth bulging at the equator. On a desk globe, how big is that bulge?

doesNotKnow: that it bulges at the equator
how small that bulge is at true scale

misconception: Either the Earth is a perfect sphere, or it is visibly squashed like in diagrams.
objective: The learner can say that the Earth's pole-to-pole diameter is about 0.3% (43 km) shorter than its equator, about 1 mm on a 30 cm globe, and that this is enough to put Chimborazo's summit farthest from the centre.

claims.text: The Earth's polar diameter is 43 km shorter than its equatorial diameter, a flattening of 0.34%.
claims.source: WGS84: semi-major axis a = 6,378.137 km, flattening f = 1/298.257223563 (NGA, WGS84 definition; from memory, not checked online). b = a(1 - f) = 6,356.752 km; 2(a - b) = 42.77 km. Computed in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: On a 30 cm globe the pole-to-pole diameter would be about 1.0 mm shorter, thinner than a coin.
claims.source: 300 mm x f = 1.006 mm, computed in Demo.tsx (GAP_MM). Coins are typically 1.3 to 2.5 mm thick (e.g. US dime 1.35 mm, euro 1 cent 1.67 mm; from memory, not checked online).

claims.text: The equator bulges out about 21 km.
Chimborazo's summit, 6,384.4 km from the Earth's centre, is farther out than Everest's, 6,382.3 km, though Everest is higher above sea level.
claims.source: Geocentric distance on the WGS84 ellipsoid computed in Demo.tsx from geodetic latitude and height: Chimborazo 1.469 S, 6,263 m; Everest 27.988 N, 8,849 m (heights and latitudes from memory: Everest 8,848.86 m by the 2020 Nepal-China survey; Chimborazo about 6,263 m; not checked online; height above ellipsoid taken as elevation, error a few tens of m from the geoid). Commonly cited figures are 6,384.4 km and 6,382.3 km (e.g. NOAA / NPR 2016 reporting; not checked).

claims.text: Textbook diagrams that show a squashed Earth exaggerate the flattening.
claims.source: Any visibly elliptical outline has a flattening far above 0.34%; at true scale the stage outline differs from a circle by 0.3 px. A framing sentence, not a survey of textbooks.

recall.question: A poster shows the Earth clearly egg-shaped, wider at the equator. What is wrong with it?
options: It exaggerates: the real bulge is about 0.3%, invisible at poster scale
Nothing: the Earth is that squashed
The bulge should be at the poles
recall.why: The polar diameter is only about 43 km (0.3%) shorter than the equator's, about 1 mm on a 30 cm globe, so a visibly squashed picture is exaggerated.
